title: Mark the survey’s margin on a monthly chart, and name the changes that pass it.
rule: A survey estimates each month’s change from a sample, so a small change can come from the sample alone. Draw the survey’s margin of error for one month’s change as a band around zero, behind the columns, and give its size, its confidence and its source in a note (Rule 14.9). The Bureau of Labor Statistics gives a 90 percent margin, so a month with no real change lands inside the band nine times in ten. The band holds for each month alone, and over many months a few can pass it by chance, so the note says that too. Name only the changes past it that the reader’s question asks about, here the drops, each with its month and value in the text’s ink (Rule 14.6), and print the full count beside them, so a reader still learns how many months fell.

Draw every month in the window the question sets, and print the window’s reason (Rule 14.10). Hatch the months still preliminary, dash the average where it includes one (Rule 14.11), and say in a note that the band does not cover the three-month average. The kit draws the phone drawing, the table and the files (Rules 14.12 to 14.14).

text: A survey of employers estimates each month’s change, and a small drop can come from the sample alone. The band shows a reader that five of the seven drops sit inside the survey’s margin, where the survey cannot tell them apart from no change, and that two pass it, so the chart names those two and still counts all seven.
why.basis: The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Employment Situation technical note, October 2026 release; Rule 14.9

builders: Draw the band with the kit’s band part from the margin the sidecar’s source line names, name the months with labels.named, and let the kit export the SVG, PNG and CSV, checked row for row against the data file.

specs.label: Window
specs.value: Every month, January 2022 to September 2026, with the reason in a note

specs.label: Margin
specs.value: A band from −122,000 to +122,000 behind the columns, with its edges, in the key and named on the drawing

specs.label: Named drops
specs.value: The two past the margin, in the text’s ink, each with its month and value

specs.label: Preliminary
specs.value: Hatched columns, the average dashed where it includes one

specs.label: Files
specs.value: The kit’s SVG, PNG and CSV, the CSV row for row with the data file

correct.caption: The monthly change in payroll jobs, all 57 months, with the survey’s margin as a band, the two drops past it named and the preliminary months hatched. Its phone drawing sits under it, then its table.

failure.caption: Fails Rule 14.142. The chart leaves out the survey’s margin of error, so all seven drops look alike, and the title states seven months of lost jobs with no word on the margin. Five of the seven sit inside the margin, where the survey cannot tell them from no change.
failure.alt: Failure case: do not publish. The same columns with no band and the seven drops drawn alike in the text’s ink, under a title that states seven months of lost jobs with no word on the margin.
failure.notes: Labeled failure: a kit figure through s-14-142-failure.chart.json (C7), its title the fault.
